session_label: Alevi transmission expansion and stubborn lead sweep
trigger: User hypothesis: multiple village/community witnesses use Hakiki poetry in Alevi ritual, so known witnesses likely scratch the surface. Task: brainstorm and proceed exhaustively to find more Jahanshah/Hakiki witness leads used in Alevi communities.
scope: Desk sweep across Alevi-Bektasi ritual manuscript literature, Ehl-i Hak/Kirklar/Ocak fieldwork literature, cenk/conk survey articles, exact incipit searches, Turkish/Azerbaijani/Persian terminology, and known catalogue surfaces. This artifact records leads and routes only; it does not alter witness counts.

known_alevi_witness_surface_before_this_: Diyarbakir Uluturk/Imam Zeynel Abidin Ocagi cenk: 8 Hakiki gazels photographed by Bulent Akin in 2016 and published by Sohrabiabad-Akin 2019.
Ilkhchi Kirklar/Celten Ocagi full divan: reported in pirs' private archive by Sohrabiabad-Akin 2019; not yet shared with academia.
Ilkhchi Kirklar/Celten Ocagi Defter/Beyaz cem conks: excerpt copies used by kelamhans in cem ritual; 3 gazels published by Sohrabiabad-Akin 2019.
Lost Diyarbakir library/divan trail: Cunbur-to-Macit report, recorded in Sohrabiabad-Akin 2019.
baseline.starting_assumption: The productive surface is not ordinary institutional title search. It is fieldwork around Alevi ocaks, dede/zakir/kelamhan private archives, and cenk/conk survey literature where Hakiki may be an unqualified mahlas inside ritual manuscripts.

web_search_clusters: Known-witness and exact-incipit confirmation: Hakiki Kelamlar, Ilkhchi Kirklar Ocagi, Her kimin musahibi yoktur, Her kimin musahibi yokdur, Vucudun sehrine girdim, Utan serm eylegil hakdan.
Alevi cenk/conk co-location: Hakiki + conk + Nesimi/Hatayi/Virani/Pir Sultan/Kul Himmet/Dede Kargin/Kececi Baba.
Turkish fieldwork: Bulent Akin, Hamidreza Sohrabiabad, Mehmet Ersal, Ozan Yilmaz, Alevi erkan conks, TUBITAK 113K056.
Azerbaijani/Iranian terminology: CahanSah Haqiqi, Heqiqi, kelam, cem, defter, cung, ocak, Kirklar, Ilkhchi, Alevi, Qizilbas.
Persian terminology: jahanshah haqiqi, haqiqi, ahl-e haqq, ilkhchi, kalam.
Catalogue/survey surfaces: DergiPark, ISAM pdfdrg, ABKED, Dogan Kaya archive pages, Turkish Bitig, Islamisation of Anatolia.

source.title: Dervis Erdal and Serhat Sabri Yilmaz, Sozlu Kultur-Yazili Kultur Iliskisi Baglaminda Conkler ve Sivas Kaynakli Bir Conk
evidence_lines_seen: Article identifies the item as an Alevi-Bektasi-origin conk preserved by Halil Esen from Suleyman Efendi of Sivas/Yildizeli/Islim.
The conk was gifted to Suleyman Efendi by a Malatya soldier friend; authors infer a Malatya-Hekimhan Alevi-Bektasi milieu because Malatya-Hekimhan and Alevi-Bektasi poets are numerous.
Poet table lists Hakiki with 1 poem, co-located with Hatayi 9, Nesimi 13, Virani 19, Pir Sultan Abdal 2, Kul Himmet 3, Sadik Baba 12, Teslim Abdal 1, Kaygusuz Abdal 1.

physical_description.holder_or_transmission: Suleyman Efendi -> son Halil Esen; given to Dervis Erdal for scholarly introduction
physical_description.provenance: Sivas, Yildizeli, Islim village; probable Malatya-Hekimhan Alevi-Bektasi recording context
physical_description.condition: some missing pages; some too faded to read; multiple hands

new_or_reinforced_leads.why_it_matters: This is a distinct Alevi-Bektasi physical witness lead outside the already-known Diyarbakir/Ilkhchi cluster. The roster is not a generic Ottoman anthology; it is a dense Alevi ritual-poet cluster with Hakiki explicitly counted.
risk_and_disambiguation: The article does not publish the Hakiki poem, incipit, folio, or attribution discussion.
Hakiki could be Jahanshah, Yusuf Hakiki, a local Alevi/Bektasi Hakiki, or another mahlas-holder.
The correct next step is text acquisition, not promotion.
followup: Contact Dervis Erdal and Serhat Sabri Yilmaz for the Hakiki folio image, incipit, and full text.
Ask whether the Hakiki item sits under a heading such as nefes, duvaz, divani, or gazel.
Compare the text against the Sohrabiabad-Akin 11 Alevi Hakiki poems, Macit/Jahanshah divan, Yusuf Hakiki corpus, and known Alevi Hakiki namesakes.
If the poem uses musahip/ikrar/erkan/murebbi/Kirklar/Shah-i Merdan lexicon or old Anatolian/Azerbaijani features, escalate to high-priority candidate.

source.title: Dogan Kaya, Alevilik Arastirmalari Dergisi 2011 article surveying 35 conks
evidence_lines_seen: The article surveys 35 conks, many from Sivas/Divrigi/Kangal/Tokat/Gurun and Alevi-Bektasi poet clusters.
Descriptions of no. 31 and no. 32 both list Hakiki among poets or mahlases.
The aggregate poet index records Hakiki (1), so the corpus contains at least one Hakiki poem even if the item-level descriptions create a count ambiguity.

candidate_items.holder: M. Sabri Koz, with photocopy in Kaya archive
candidate_items.contents_signal: nefesler, ilahiler, semailer, gazels, qitas, many mufreds and anonymous poems; poet list includes Hakiki alongside Dervis Ali, Fahri, Gevheri, Hudai, Katibi, Niyazi, Seyyidi, Uftade, etc.
candidate_items.priority: medium: mixed tekke/asik list, but direct text can resolve cheaply

candidate_items.contents_signal: nefes, divan, gazel and beyit; Hakiki appears with Fuzuli, Garib, Hatayi, Kaygusuz Sultan, Kul Himmet, Kul Nesimi, Pir Sultan Abdal, Sersem Abdal, Teslim Abdal, Turabi, Virani Abdal and other Alevi-Bektasi names.
candidate_items.priority: high: stronger Alevi-Bektasi co-location than no. 31

new_or_reinforced_leads.why_it_matters: This is the most concrete new archive route after the Sivas Islim conk: at least one Hakiki poem is indexed inside a known Alevi conk survey corpus, and two item descriptions point to candidate conks.
risk_and_disambiguation: The article gives no poem text or folio for Hakiki.
The aggregate index count of Hakiki (1) conflicts with two item-level mentions; one mention may be a duplicate, catalogue slip, or a single poem copied across notes.
Late Alevi/Bektasi conks can contain non-Jahanshah Hakiki namesakes.
followup: Contact Dogan Kaya or locate his archive access path for conk nos. 31 and 32.
Contact M. Sabri Koz for no. 31 and Lutfu Segmen or associated heirs/archives for no. 32.
Request only the Hakiki item first: folio/page, first and last couplets, heading, meter, nearby poems, and image if possible.

source.title: Bulent Akin, Ehl-i Haklarda Kelamhanlik Gelenegi ve Kelamhan Defterlerinin Gelenegin Korunmasi ve Aktarimindaki Rolu
evidence_lines_seen: Kelam means sacred poem read in cem, not ordinarily performed outside the belief circle.
Kelams are preserved in Defter manuscripts, described as conk or mecmua-type written records.
Kelam contents differ by hanedan, ocak or taife.
Conclusion explicitly names Iranian Kirklar, Aliilahiler and other Alevi communities as needing comparative study with Turkey/Balkan Alevi-Bektasi manuscript traditions.

new_or_reinforced_leads.why_it_matters: This source does not add a Jahanshah witness by itself, but it explains exactly where hidden witnesses would live: kelamhan defters, ocak/hanedan/taife archives, and ritual manuscripts not exposed through ordinary library catalogues.
new_or_reinforced_leads.false_positive_warning: Hakiki makam and Hakiki kelam can be generic Ehl-i Hak terms for sacred/true makams or kelams, not necessarily the poet Hakiki. Treat them as route terms unless paired with Cihan/Jahanshah, mahlas context, poem incipit, or a manuscript item.

source.title: Akbar Najaf, Qaraqoyunlu hokmdari Cahansah Haqiqinin yeni tapilan seirleri
evidence_lines_seen: Keywords include Haqiqi, qizilbas, elevi, xalq islami, cung, defter, cem, ocak.
The article explicitly cites Sohrabiabad-Akin 2019 as the source for the Diyarbakir cenk and Ilkhchi Kirklar Defter/Beyaz evidence.
The body republishes the 8 Diyarbakir and 3 Ilkhchi Hakiki ghazals in Azerbaijani orthography; no independent manuscript source is named beyond Sohrabiabad-Akin 2019.

new_or_reinforced_leads.why_it_matters: This is not an independent witness because it depends on Sohrabiabad-Akin 2019, but it is more than a keyword bridge: it republishes the known Alevi Hakiki poem set in Azerbaijani orthography and gives searchable terminology that can reach non-Turkish discussions: cung, defter, cem, ocak, qizilbas, elevi, Haqiqi.
new_or_reinforced_leads.followup: If Najaf is used in an apparatus, compare its orthographic text against Sohrabiabad-Akin 2019 Ek-1/Ek-2 before treating it as variant evidence; ask Najaf only if there is reason to suspect access to a source beyond the cited 2019 article.

source.title: Dogan Kaya, Bir Conk Sekiz Sair
evidence_lines_seen: Poet roster includes Hakiki and Nesimi among 21 identified poets.
The article transcribes rare poets, not the Hakiki poem.

deprioritized_or_negative_hits.interpretation: Useful as a public institutional conk lead, but not currently evidence of Alevi community use. The roster is broadly religious/sufi rather than a dense Hatayi/Pir Sultan/Kul Himmet/Virani Alevi cluster.
deprioritized_or_negative_hits.followup: Low-cost if Suleymaniye images can be requested: identify Hakiki folio and incipit. Do not prioritize over Sivas Islim or Kaya nos. 31/32.

source.title: Omur Ceylan and Mehmet Ersal, Alevi-Bektasi Kultur Enstitusu Arsivi Yazma Eserler Katalogu I
evidence_lines_seen: The catalogue introduces an Alevi-Bektasi Culture Institute archive built from personal Alevi-Bektasi manuscript archives and digital collections.
The first catalogue article describes many conks, but text search in this session did not find Hakiki.

deprioritized_or_negative_hits.interpretation: No new Hakiki hit from Catalog I, but the archive is structurally high value. Later catalogue installments or uncatalogued holdings should be searched directly.
Exact incipit searches mainly rediscovered Sohrabiabad-Akin and derivative secondary pages; no independent web-visible witness surfaced.
Rediscovered known Islamisation/Anatolia DB Cihansah/Hagigi surfaces but did not add an Alevi-community witness beyond prior corpus coverage.

false_positive_classes_reinforced.description: In Ehl-i Hak/Alevi music and ritual literature, hakiki can mark sacred/true kelams or makams. It is a route term, not author evidence, unless there is a mahlas, byline, Cihan/Jahanshah co-occurrence, or poem text.

Late conks often contain unqualified Hakiki inside mixed asik/tekke rosters. Alevi co-location raises priority but does not by itself prove Jahanshah. Require incipit, language features, doctrinal lexicon, or comparison with known Jahanshah/Yusuf/local corpora.
A large anthology may contain Hakiki, Nesimi, Hatayi, and Shah Ismail far apart. Only local folio-level adjacency or shared ritual section matters.

operational_followup_plan.ask: Obtain Hakiki poem folio/image/transcription from Dervis Erdal or Serhat Sabri Yilmaz; use Mehmet Ersal as a parallel Cumhuriyet University / Alevi-Bektasi manuscript contact route if direct author contact stalls.
operational_followup_plan.acceptance_criteria: At least incipit, explicit/mahlas line, heading, folio, and neighboring poems.

operational_followup_plan.ask: Resolve which conk contains the aggregate Hakiki (1) poem and obtain text/image.
operational_followup_plan.acceptance_criteria: Identify no. 31 vs no. 32, holder, folio, item type (full poem vs beyit/mufret), incipit, explicit, and immediate context.

operational_followup_plan.target: Kirklar/Celten Ocagi and Ilkhchi kelamhan network
operational_followup_plan.ask: Through Bulent Akin/Sohrabiabad, request metadata-only survey first: number of Hakiki poems in the full divan and Defter/Beyaz copies, whether copies exist in more than one household, and whether headings/incipits can be shared.
operational_followup_plan.acceptance_criteria: Count of distinct physical items and non-sensitive incipit list; no need to demand full ritual texts initially.

operational_followup_plan.target: Alevi-Bektasi Culture Institute archive and Mehmet Ersal fieldwork corpus
operational_followup_plan.ask: Search beyond Catalog I for Hakiki/Haqiqi in conk contents, especially uncatalogued or later catalogued items from Amasya, Kirikkale, Corum, Cankiri, Ankara, Eskisehir, Isparta, Didymoteicho/Rousa and Momchilgrad/Bulgaria.
operational_followup_plan.acceptance_criteria: Any item-level Hakiki occurrence with conk number, owner/archive, folio, and neighboring poets.

operational_followup_plan.ask: Use the confirmed Imam Zeynel Abidin, Seyyid Dervis Ali, Abbas Onen, and Bektas Onbasi trails to locate related dede/zakir conks not yet published; do not use any AguiCen/Agucan-style lead until the exact ocak name and source are verified.
operational_followup_plan.acceptance_criteria: Inventory of conks/divans that include Hakiki, Fuzuli, Seyyid Nizamoglu, Nesimi, Hatayi or ritual section headings.

operational_followup_plan.ask: Submit a low-cost institutional image or folio-identification request for the Hakiki item surfaced by Dogan Kaya's Bir Conk Sekiz Sair article.
operational_followup_plan.acceptance_criteria: Determine Hakiki folio, item type, incipit, explicit, and local neighboring poems; close as wrong-Hakiki if the text is a namesake.

summary.strongest_new_candidate: Sivas/Yildizeli Islim Suleyman Efendi conk: Alevi-Bektasi source, probable Malatya-Hekimhan transmission, one Hakiki poem in a dense Alevi poet roster.
summary.strongest_archive_route: Dogan Kaya 35-conk corpus, especially conk no. 32 with Hakiki in a Hatayi/Kul Himmet/Kul Nesimi/Pir Sultan/Teslim/Turabi/Virani Abdal cluster.
summary.main_methodological_result: For Alevi-community Jahanshah witnesses, fieldwork bibliographies and conk survey articles now outperform YEK/Google catalogue mining. The next breakthrough likely requires asking targeted holders for a single Hakiki folio rather than broad public search.
